A research offer is a beginning, not the whole plan.

Study and research can open a way to Australia. Before anyone books a flight, make space for the visa, the people moving with you, the money, and the first weeks on the ground.

Start with the family rules

If a partner or family member is coming, check this first.

Rules for including family on Student visa applications changed on 2 October 2026. Family generally cannot be included unless a limited exemption applies. Current Student visa holders cannot add family after the visa is granted. PhD students are among the exemption categories, but the main applicant still needs to meet the applicable criteria.

Read the current family member rules
Open Path source review: 13 October 2026

Put the moving parts in a useful order.

You do not need every answer on day one. These are the questions that help turn an exciting opportunity into a plan you can check.

01

Get the study details in writing

Confirm the course or research program, provider, start date, funding, and the documents the institution expects. An offer or scholarship is not the same as a visa grant.

Check the Student visa information
02

Work out who is part of the move

If a partner or child plans to come, read the latest family rules before building the rest of the plan around that assumption. Confirm any exemption against the official criteria and the main applicant's circumstances.

See who may be included
03

Build your own document plan

Use the live application instructions as your checklist. Depending on the case, preparation may involve identity, study, financial, health, character, or relationship documents. The evidence requested is not identical for everyone.

In our own application, we gathered records from Nigeria and other places we had lived, along with relationship evidence and health checks. That was our experience, not a universal list.

Open the document planner
04

Budget for the whole household

Look beyond tuition or the scholarship. Check the visa and application costs, health cover, travel, housing, local transport, and the time it may take to settle into work and daily life.

Understand health insurance requirements
05

Plan the first month, not just arrival day

Think about temporary accommodation, getting to campus, phone access, opening a bank account, and what needs to happen before your first pay or stipend. You can set these up gradually, but a short list helps.

Open the first month checklist

The official process is only part of the move.

We arrived with the big decisions behind us and a new set of small ones ahead: finding a place, figuring out transport, and making a home one step at a time. Open Path is being built for both parts of the journey.
